narrative_profile: Psychological thriller with supernatural and medical procedural elements; slow-burn suspense; locked single POV; tone of dread and restraint.
surface_case: A haunted-machine ghost story: an old printer in a dying ER predicts who will die, and the nurse races each night to beat its predictions and save people.
true_case: The machine isn't prophetic. It prints the name of whoever the nurse will let die that night through a clinical decision. It doesn't see the future — it reflects her own hand. Every prediction she tries to fight, she causes by fighting it. The final slip prints her own name.
core_question: Does the machine foresee, or choose?
emotional_question: Can Iris Callahan reconcile the guilt of the patient she lost a year ago — and accept that her own choices, not fate, determine what happens on her watch?
book1_promise: A slow-burn psychological thriller where a night-shift nurse races to beat a death-predicting machine — only to discover that her resistance is the very thing that causes the deaths she tries to prevent. Each chapter ends with a hook that tightens the dread until the final, devastating slip.
book2_hook: The next morning an identical label printer is delivered to the ER — still sealed in its box, shipped from the very hospital where Marguerite worked 30 years ago. It isn't plugged in. It has already printed one slip.
reader_payoff_book1: Iris's emotional and moral resolution — she accepts responsibility for her past and breaks the cycle of resistance, earning a moment of peace before the next threat arrives.
